transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-01-30 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 mins
- Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Kalypso ML Ops), Daniel (Kalypso Platform), Leila (Kalypso CTO)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: quick intake — Kalypso runs mixed batch + real time inference for clinical summarization. Interested in reserved capacity with strong isolation for certain tenants that process PHI-adjacent data, plus burst capability for spikes after nightly data loads.
Topics: reserved nodes, hotpool prewarm, VPC/on-prem path, KMS / audit logs, latency targets (p50/p95/p99)

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: ok hey everyone great to meet you, thanks for carving out the time, quick intro — I'm Ethan, account exec on Redwood.
[00:06] Marta: hi Ethan, hi Priya, thanks, i'm Marta — i run MLOps at Kalypso, onboarded a few model endpoints last quarter.
[00:11] Priya: hey all, Priya, I'm the solutions engineer — i'll be the technical lead on sizing and performance.
[00:16] Leila: Leila here — CTO, i'll be listening for compliance implications and cost tradeoffs.
[00:20] Daniel: Dan, platform eng — i'll handle network and infra questions.

[00:30] Ethan: quick agenda — baseline traffic, isolation needs, burst patterns, compliance/gov, and next steps. does that work?
[00:35] Marta: yes, perfect. we're evaluating three options: Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated reserved GPUs, or a private VPC deployment. leaning toward Dedicated if we can get deterministic latency and tenant isolation.

[02:05] Priya: can you walk through the workload shape — what percent realtime vs batch, typical seq lengths, token profiles?
[02:12] Marta: sure. daytime is low qps realtime — like 40-60 requests/min for chat assistants (short prompts ~150 tokens). then nightly batch where we re-run summarization on 200k docs, that's heavy, big seq lengths up to 2k tokens and long tails. spikes usually after ETL jobs finish at 02:00 local and certain clinical events where many requests come in simultaneously. we want that not to blow up latency.

[04:40] Priya: ok so mixed profile. question on isolation — do you need physical node isolation per customer or is logical tenant fencing fine?
[04:48] Marta: for internal teams that touch PHI-ish records, legal wants guaranteed no co-tenancy with other customers and auditable logs. maybe we need dedicated node pools for them. for public-facing features, shared nodes could be ok.
[05:12] Leila: to be clear: we prefer Dedicated reserved pools for the PHI-adjacent tenants. if Redwood can provide audit logs, KMS integration, and VPC peering, Private isn't required initially.

[06:00] Daniel: networking thing — we run in AWS us-east-1, have strict egress rules and our VPCs use shared services. if we go Dedicated, can we still peer and control routing?
[06:10] Priya: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering in our Private flavor; for hosted dedicated we provide secure endpoints + VPC peering options; we can detail exact subnet/CIDR requirements. there are also firewall rules and private link options.

[08:00] Marta: SLA and latency SLOs — we need p99 < 800ms for our realtime routes, p95 < 250ms ideally. batch can be best-effort. does Redwood have verification for p99 under burst?
[08:12] Priya: we typically size reserved pools for steady-state throughput and then allow warm pools/hot nodes for bursts. p99 depends on model size and batching. for small chat models that's achievable; for 2k-length batch tokens p99 is higher. we can prototype with your traffic profile to estimate.

[09:45] Ethan: pricing & commitment question — do you have an internal budget or procurement window?
[09:50] Leila: fiscal Q2 commit; budget not finalized but we need a ballpark to compare to CloudX managed endpoints.
[10:10] Ethan: we'll send a reserved capacity worksheet and a comparative TCO note.

[11:30] Daniel: burst behavior — if nightly batch spikes saturate nodes, do you have automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants or lower-priority queues?
[11:40] Priya: yes, Redwood supports policy routing: fallback to quantized variant, or route to lower-cost region, or queue with graceful degradation. also prefix/KV caching helps reduce recompute. for heavy batch runs we recommend separate burst-only node pool to avoid affecting realtime.

[13:05] Marta: are there limits on prewarm/hotpool capacity? We want to prewarm N GPUs before the 02:00 window.
[13:12] Priya: reserved pools can have warm pools — customer-configurable prewarm targets. constraints based on committed GPU count; you can reserve a hotpool percentage and allowed burst credits for short spikes.

[15:00] Leila: security — SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM, audit logs, and ability to restrict token storage. do you support customer-managed keys?
[15:12] Priya: yes, we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private plans; audit logs are available in the console and can be exported to your SIEM. we'll link the SOC2 report and a compliance pack.

[17:30] Marta: curious about preemption and multi-tenancy blast radius — if we host other customers on the same GPU nodes will noisy neighbors affect us?
[17:38] Priya: isolation is managed via tenant fencing — process-level isolation plus cgroups for GPU. for PHI tenants we recommend dedicated pools to eliminate cross-customer noisy neighbors.

[19:00] Ethan: any regulatory constraints about data residency?
[19:04] Marta: we're primarily US-based but partner clinics in EU — may need the Private deployment for EU workloads later. for now US-only.

[20:30] Daniel: integration — how does rolling deploys and model versioning work on Dedicated?
[20:38] Priya: same API surface — you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts; console shows per-model metrics and per-route cost breakdowns. during upgrades we support canary traffic split and automatic fallback.

[22:00] Marta: we run custom tokenization pipeline and need custom kernels for some ops — any constraints on bringing custom ops?
[22:10] Priya: in Dedicated/Private you can request custom runtime layers; in hosted we limit custom kernel uploads for security. we can surface a process for validating and whitelisting ops.

[25:00] Leila: performance validation — we want Redwood to run a short benchmark with our representative payloads. what's the usual turnaround?
[25:08] Priya: if you share a 7-day histogram and sample payloads we'll aim for a 5-business-day proof-of-performance estimate; if you want an iso bench with p99 targets we can schedule a dedicated pilot window.

[27:40] Marta: procurement — we'll need contract language about uptime SLA and data handling. do you offer enterprise add-ons for longer log retention?
[27:50] Ethan: yes we have add-ons for observability retention and enterprise SLAs. we'll surface contract terms with the pricing worksheet.

[30:00] Daniel: curious — how do you support burst across regions? if us-east saturates can you route to us-west?
[30:08] Priya: smart routing policies support region fallback; you can set cost vs latency policy to prefer local region then fallback. also model variants in other regions can be used.

[33:00] Marta: edge case: what happens if a nightly batch starts saturating and pushes micro-bursts during day — will that starve realtime?
[33:08] Priya: recommended pattern is segregation: host batch in separate node pool with capped concurrency and non-preemptive quotas for realtime pools. we can set burst guardrails and QoS rules.

[36:30] Ethan: any competitive concerns? do you evaluate Anthropic or CloudX?
[36:35] Leila: we did a PoC with CloudX — cheaper for small models but lacks the audit / warm pool controls. Anthropic had good latency but vendor lock-in concerns. so cost/perf + compliance matters for us.

[38:00] Marta: success criteria — deterministic p99 for realtime, dedicated isolation for PHI teams, ability to run nightly batch without impacting realtime, and a pilot with 2-week validation. timeline: procurement early Q2.

[40:20] Priya: recap on technical asks: 1) sizing estimate for reserved GPUs to serve daytime realtime + nightly batch, 2) prewarm plan for 02:00 ET job (how many hot nodes and warm pools), 3) network/VPC peering checklist, 4) SOC2/KMS docs.

[41:00] Ethan: i'll own commercial followup — send pricing sheet, SE — send capacity worksheet and plan for bench.

[42:15] Marta: good, please include sample SLAs and an outline of onboarding steps.

[43:00] Leila: one last — can you show a quick sketch of fallback options (quantized model routing, lower-cost region) in the doc you send?
[43:10] Priya: yes will include fallback sketches and tradeoff notes.

[44:00] Ethan: excellent — thanks all. we'll follow up with the three deliverables and schedule pilot planning next week.

End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript with occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "prewarm" transcribed as "pre-worm" in a few spots) and generic speaker markers.
